Test Description: Validate default reset values and read/write behavior of GPIO_8 to GPIO_27 registers over the AHB register interface using predefined read/write masks and multiple data patterns. Non-readable or non-writable registers are skipped per masks; expected readback accounts for preserved default bits where writes are masked off.
Meta Test Description: The test verifies default values and R/W functionality for a set of GPIO registers listed in addr_array (GPIO_8..GPIO_27). It first runs chk_rst_val(): for each address i in [0..CNT-1], it skips if skip_rst_array[i]==1; if read_mask_array[i]==0x00000000, it skips as not readable. Otherwise it performs data_rd = read_reg(addr_array[i]) and masks with 0xfffffffe to ignore bit0, then compares against default_value_array[i]; on mismatch increments def_fail_cnt and logs failure. Next, chk_rd_wr(): defines six patterns {0xffffffff, 0xaaaaaaaa, 0x55555555, 0xf5f5f5f5, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xffff0000}. For each pattern, it writes (data_wr & write_mask_array[i]) to each address i that is not skipped (skip_array[i]==0) and is writable (write_mask_array[i]!=0). It then reads back for each address i that is not skipped, writable, and readable (read_mask_array[i]!=0) using data_rd = read_reg(addr) & read_mask_array[i]. Expected exp_val is computed as: (data_wr & read_mask_array[i] & write_mask_array[i]) | ((~write_mask_array[i]) & read_mask_array[i] & default_value_array[i]). It compares data_rd with exp_val; on mismatch increments wr_fail_cnt and logs. At the end of test_case(), if def_fail_cnt>0 or wr_fail_cnt>0 calls finish(1) else finish(0). A soft_reset_chk() routine exists but is compiled out (#ifdef 0).
Remarks: Default value check intentionally masks bit0 to avoid false mismatches due to input sampling behavior. Registers with read mask of 0 are treated as non-readable and skipped; registers with write mask of 0 are treated as non-writable and skipped. Expected readback preserves default bits where writes are masked off. Ensure that the iteration count matches the size of the control arrays to avoid out-of-bounds access. When inputs are not forced, some input bits may read high; forcing zero can affect level selection and lead to mismatches, hence the mask of bit0 in default check.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Initialize the GPIO register list (GPIO_8 through GPIO_27) with associated default, read-mask, and write-mask data.
2) Default value verification: For each GPIO register that is readable and not marked to skip, read the register and compare its value (with bit0 ignored) against the documented default value. Record any mismatches.
3) Write/read verification: For each of the six data patterns, write the pattern masked by each register’s write mask to all writable, non-skipped GPIO registers; then read back the value masked by each register’s read mask and compare against the expected value computed from the written bits plus preserved default bits where writes are masked. Record any mismatches.
4) Determine pass/fail: If no default or write/read mismatches were recorded, declare PASS; otherwise, declare FAIL.
Impacted Registers: GPIO_8, GPIO_9, GPIO_10, GPIO_11, GPIO_12, GPIO_13, GPIO_14, GPIO_15, GPIO_16, GPIO_17, GPIO_18, GPIO_19, GPIO_20, GPIO_21, GPIO_22, GPIO_23, GPIO_24, GPIO_25, GPIO_26, GPIO_27
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: PASS if, for all GPIO_8–GPIO_27: (a) the default read value (with bit0 ignored) matches the documented default when readable; and (b) for each test pattern, the masked readback equals (written_bits & write_mask & read_mask) OR (preserved_default_bits & ~write_mask & read_mask). Any mismatch results in FAIL.
Meta Test Steps / Procedure:
test_case():
- Call chk_rst_val(). If DEBUG_DISPLAY, print end banner.
- Call chk_rd_wr(). If DEBUG_DISPLAY, print end banner.
- If (def_fail_cnt > 0 || wr_fail_cnt > 0) finish(1) else finish(0).

chk_rst_val():
- For i=0..CNT-1:
  - addr = addr_array[i].
  - If skip_rst_array[i] == 1: (optionally log) continue.
  - If read_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000: (optionally log) continue.
  - data_rd = read_reg(addr).
  - data = (data_rd & 0xfffffffe) // ignore bit0 in default check.
  - If data == default_value_array[i]: (optionally log PASS); else { def_fail_cnt++; log failure with addr, expected, and read data }.

chk_rd_wr():
- Define chk_val[6] = {0xffffffff,0xaaaaaaaa,0x55555555,0xf5f5f5f5,0xA5A5A5A5,0xffff0000}.
- For each j in 0..5:
  - data_wr = chk_val[j].
  - Write phase: for i=0..CNT-1: addr = addr_array[i]; if skip_array[i]==1 continue; if write_mask_array[i]==0 continue; else write_reg(addr, (data_wr & write_mask_array[i])).
  - Read/verify phase: for i=0..CNT-1: addr = addr_array[i]; if skip_array[i]==1 continue; if write_mask_array[i]==0 continue; if read_mask_array[i]==0 continue; else {
    data_rd = (read_reg(addr) & read_mask_array[i]);
    wr_n = (write_mask_array[i] ^ 0xffffffff);
    exp_val = ((data_wr & read_mask_array[i] & write_mask_array[i]) | (wr_n & read_mask_array[i] & default_value_array[i]));
    if (data_rd == exp_val) { (optionally log PASS) } else { wr_fail_cnt++; log failure with addr, expected, read } }.

Feature: interrupts can be generated based on positive edge or negative edge or level high or level low detection at GPIO input
Test Description: Verify per-pin negative-edge GPIO interrupts by enabling each pin’s interrupt, generating a falling edge on the corresponding pad, checking group interrupt status, and clearing both per-pin raw and system raw status via the GPIO and system interrupt registers.
Meta Test Description:
test_case(): Initialize test_err=0. If compiled for GPIO0, enable GIC IRQ 87; if for GPIO1, enable GIC IRQ 88. Enable system-level GPIO interrupt output by writing to INTR_EN1 with the respective GPIO0/1 enable bit. Set external pad control at 0xA0243ffc to 0xFFFFFFFF (drive high). For i=0..31: compute addr1 = (MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + i*4); write_reg(addr1, (1u<<20)|(1u<<18)|(1u<<16)); wait_on(10). For i=0..31: wr_val = (1u<<i); write_reg(gpio_intr_raw_stclr1, wr_val) to clear raw status; write_reg(INTR1_INTR_EN1, wr_val) to enable interrupt for that pin; wait_on(10); set int_pend=1; drive 0xA0243ffc to 0xFFFFFFFF, wait_on(30), then write 0xA0243ffc with bitwise NOT of wr_val to create a falling edge on the selected pad; poll with timeout=5000 while (int_pend) with wait_on(10); on timeout expiry, log timeout for GPIO(i+8) and increment test_err. Call finish(test_err).

Default_IRQHandler(): local_wr=(1u<<i); set int_pend=0; drive 0xA0243ffc to 0xFFFFFFFF (restore high). Read per-pin register raddr=(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + i*4) into rdata. If ((rdata & 0x1)!=0) then test_err++. If ((rdata & 0x2)!=0x0) then read group status rdata_grp=read_reg(INTR1_INTR_STS1); if ((rdata_grp & local_wr)==0) test_err++; write per-pin clear/config at raddr2=(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + i*4) with (1u<<20)|(1u<<16); write_reg(gpio_intr_raw_stclr1, local_wr); read back rdata_grp=read_reg(INTR1_INTR_STS1); if (rdata_grp!=0) test_err++; Then clear system raw status: if GPIO0 build, write RAW_STCR1 with GPIO0 bit and GIC_ClearIRQ(87); if GPIO1 build, write RAW_STCR1 with GPIO1 bit and GIC_ClearIRQ(88). Else (if (rdata & 0x2)==0) increment test_err.
Remarks: Ensure system interrupt output is enabled via INTR_EN1 and the correct GIC interrupt (87/88) is enabled before generating edges. Clear raw status in gpio_intr_raw_stclr1 before enabling per-pin interrupts to avoid stale pending states. External pad drive at 0xA0243ffc must correctly control the GPIO lines under test. After servicing an interrupt, clear RAW_STCR1 to release the system-level raw status.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1) Enable the system interrupt output for the target GPIO instance using INTR_EN1 and enable the corresponding GIC interrupt (87 for GPIO0, 88 for GPIO1). 2) Drive the external pad control at 0xA0243ffc high to set a known idle level. 3) Configure each per-pin GPIO control register for GPIO_8–GPIO_39 to enable negative-edge detection and clear any pending raw status. 4) For each pin: clear its raw status in gpio_intr_raw_stclr1, enable its interrupt in INTR1_INTR_EN1, then generate a falling edge by toggling the external pad control; wait for the ISR to service without hitting the timeout. 5) In the ISR: verify the per-pin status indicates an edge occurred, confirm the corresponding bit is set in INTR1_INTR_STS1, clear per-pin raw status and group raw status, verify INTR1_INTR_STS1 is cleared, and clear RAW_STCR1; acknowledge the GIC interrupt. 6) Pass the test if all pins complete without timeouts and all status checks and clears succeed.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: PASS if each pin (GPIO_8–GPIO_39) generates a negative-edge interrupt when driven from high to low, the respective group status bit in INTR1_INTR_STS1 sets during service, and both the per-pin raw status and group/system raw statuses are cleared successfully (no timeouts and no error increments).

Test Description: Verify that enabling positive-edge interrupts on GPIO pads generates an interrupt on a rising edge for each pin, asserts the group interrupt status, and that per-pin raw and system raw status can be cleared correctly.
Meta Test Description: The test enables system-level GPIO interrupt output and configures GPIO pads for positive-edge detection. Group IO control registers are used to set GPIO pads in input mode. Group interrupt enable is asserted so per-pin events propagate to the interrupt controller. For each pin in the test set, a rising edge is generated on the corresponding pad; the ISR validates per-pin status and group status, then clears the per-pin raw status via the raw status clear register and also clears the system raw status register before re-enabling group interrupt if masked during service. The test passes if all pins generate an interrupt on a rising edge and all status bits are cleared correctly with no timeouts.
Remarks: Ensure GPIO pads are configured to input mode using the group IO control registers before generating edges. System interrupt output must be enabled prior to testing. Clear raw status prior to enabling per-pin interrupts to avoid stale pending states. After servicing, clear both the per-pin raw status and the system raw status to prevent re-entry.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1) Enable system-level GPIO interrupt output and the corresponding GIC interrupt for the GPIO instance. 2) Configure all relevant GPIO pads to input mode using the group IO control registers. 3) Enable positive-edge interrupt detection for each GPIO pin and enable the group interrupt output. 4) For each GPIO pin under test, generate a single rising edge on the pad. 5) In the ISR, verify the per-pin interrupt indication and that the group interrupt status bit is set; then clear the per-pin raw status and the system raw status. 6) Re-enable group interrupt output if it was masked during service and proceed to the next pin. 7) Pass if all pins generate interrupts on rising edges and all status bits clear correctly without timeouts.
Impacted Registers: GPIO_8 (and subsequent per-pin control registers for the tested range), gp0_intr2_intr_en1, INTR1_INTR_STS1, GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP1, GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP2, GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP3, GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP4, INTR_EN1, RAW_STCR1, GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: PASS if, for each configured GPIO pin, a rising edge triggers an interrupt, the corresponding group status bit sets, and both the per-pin raw status and the system raw status are cleared successfully in the ISR without timeouts. Any missing interrupt, incorrect status, or uncleared status results in FAIL.
Meta Impacted Registers: MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 (+ per-pin stride), MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1, MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1, MIZAR_GPIO_GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP1, MIZAR_GPIO_GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP2, MIZAR_GPIO_GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP3, MIZAR_GPIO_GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP4, MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1, MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1, MIZAR_GPIO_GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1
Meta Validation / Acceptance Criteria: During ISR handling for a given pin i: INTR1_INTR_STS1 must report the bit corresponding to i as set upon entry; after writing the pin bit to GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1, INTR1_INTR_STS1 must read 0 for the cleared condition; RAW_STCR1 write must clear the system raw status for the GPIO block; no timeout should occur while waiting for ISR completion. Final result is PASS if all pins meet these checks, otherwise FAIL.
